+"""Delivery-mode renderers: image_pull compose + per-mode Makefile.
+
+`image_pull` must produce a **standalone** compose file with no `build:` keys
+anywhere: an override merged onto the root compose cannot express "don't
+build" (Compose merges mappings, so the base `build:` keys survive), and
+`up --build` would still build from source. `source_build` keeps the root
+compose but gets a Makefile pinning the exact invocations `install.sh` uses
+(SPEC-072726-3439 Phase 2).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import copy
+import subprocess
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+DEFAULT_IMAGE_REPOSITORY = "ghcr.io/blakematthews-dev"
+DEFAULT_IMAGE_TAG = "latest"
+
+# Services in the root compose that carry build: keys, mapped to their
+# published image names. Digest pins are injected by the release workflow
+# (Phase 5) — until then these tags are placeholders and install.sh falls
+# back to source_build unless MAISTRO_IMAGE_PULL_READY=1.
+PINNED_IMAGES: dict[str, str] = {
+    "maistro-engine": f"{DEFAULT_IMAGE_REPOSITORY}/maistro-engine:{DEFAULT_IMAGE_TAG}",
+    "hive-conductor": f"{DEFAULT_IMAGE_REPOSITORY}/hive-conductor:{DEFAULT_IMAGE_TAG}",
+}
+
+
+def render_image_pull_compose(
+    base_compose: dict[str, Any], images: dict[str, str] | None = None
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Return a standalone compose document with every build: replaced by image:.
+
+    Raises if a built service has no pinned image mapping — silently keeping
+    its build: key would reintroduce the source build this mode exists to
+    avoid.
+    """
+    image_map = {**PINNED_IMAGES, **(images or {})}
+    doc = copy.deepcopy(base_compose)
+    services = doc.get("services")
+    if not isinstance(services, dict):
+        raise ValueError("base compose has no services mapping")
+    for name, svc in services.items():
+        if not isinstance(svc, dict) or "build" not in svc:
+            continue
+        if name not in image_map:
+            raise ValueError(f"no pinned image for built service {name!r}")
+        svc.pop("build")
+        svc["image"] = image_map[name]
+    return doc
+
+
+def git_revision(repo_root: Path) -> str | None:
+    try:
+        out = subprocess.run(
+            ["git", "-C", str(repo_root), "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
+            capture_output=True,
+            text=True,
+            check=False,
+            timeout=10,
+        )
+    except OSError:
+        return None
+    rev = out.stdout.strip()
+    return rev if out.returncode == 0 and rev else None
+
+
+def render_makefile(
+    mode: str,
+    *,
+    base_compose_path: str | None,
+    revision: str | None,
+) -> str:
+    """Operator-facing Makefile wrapping the exact compose invocations.
+
+    Recipes must be tab-indented — keep literal tabs in this template.
+    """
+    # --project-directory pins interpolation (.env) and relative bind-mount
+    # resolution to the repo root, not this artifacts directory.
+    project_dir = "."
+    if base_compose_path:
+        parent = str(Path(base_compose_path).parent)
+        project_dir = parent if parent not in ("", ".") else "."
+    if mode == "image_pull":
+        compose = f"docker compose --project-directory {project_dir} -f compose.install.yml"
+        up = f"{compose} up -d"
+        update = f"{compose} pull\n\t{up}"
+    else:
+        base = base_compose_path or "<path-to-docker-compose.yml>"
+        compose = (
+            f"docker compose --project-directory {project_dir} -f {base} -f compose.override.yml"
+        )
+        up = f"{compose} up -d --build"
+        update = up
+    rev_line = f"# source revision: {revision}" if revision else "# source revision: (unknown)"
+    return f"""# Generated by maistro-install — delivery_mode={mode}
+{rev_line}
+# Runtime behavior is identical across delivery modes; only how the
+# maistro-engine and hive-conductor images arrive differs.
+
+.PHONY: install up down logs status backup teardown update
+
+install:
+\t{compose} config --quiet
+\t@echo "compose config OK — run 'make up'"
+
+up:
+\t{up}
+
+down:
+\t{compose} down
+
+logs:
+\t{compose} logs -f --tail=200
+
+status:
+\t{compose} ps
+
+backup:
+\t{compose} exec postgres pg_dump -U maistro maistro > maistro-backup-$$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).sql
+
+teardown:
+\t@echo "This deletes all volumes (database, conductor state). Ctrl-C to abort."
+\t@sleep 5
+\t{compose} down -v
+
+update:
+\t{update}
+"""

+    written: list[Path] = []

+    makefile.write_text(
+        render_makefile(mode, base_compose_path=base_compose_path, revision=revision),

+    written.append(makefile)

fix(security): close the harness blind spot, drop the inert YAML knob

Four follow-ups from the adversarial review of this batch.

1. Corrected the I6 citation. The test body is at
   formal/models/test_sentinel_policy.py:221-223, not 219-221 (219 is the
   closing paren, 220 the @settings decorator). The wrong range had been
   baked into the ADR's labelled code block and this module's docstring,
   where it would have become the canonical pointer to the invariant.

2. testing/harness.py was a second container-assembly path that
   hardcoded Gate(warden=warden) and permission_table = {} while
   accepting an AgentConfig it never consulted. A test could set
   permission_preset and silently observe pre-fix behaviour -- the same
   'parallel assembly drifts from the real one' shape that let the empty
   table and missing tracker survive a green suite in the first place. It
   now mirrors create_container, and two new tests pin both the armed and
   default cases, since a fix for 'nothing catches this' that nothing
   catches has the same defect.

3. Removed permission_preset / strike_tracking_enabled from
   config/settings.py SecurityConfig. Nothing reads
   MaistroYamlConfig.security -- verified by attribute-level grep; the
   four fields already there are declared-but-inert -- so those knobs
   would have let an operator set a security setting in maistro.yaml and
   watch it do nothing. That is the defect this batch exists to fix, and
   shipping it in the same commit would have been incoherent. A comment
   records the precondition: wire MaistroYamlConfig -> AgentConfig first.

4. Qualified the no-change claim. It is true of the permission table and
   the strike tracker; H12's Warden binding is ungated and does change
   default skill-import behaviour, though only by surfacing warden:* flags
   in scan_issues -- it cannot produce a new denial, since blocking comes
   from fix_content unfixables and security_scan, and scan_issues has no
   consumers outside the pipeline.

Verified: core suite 5630 passed / 1 skipped / 1 xfailed -- the harness
change touches 34 call sites and broke none. Batch 2 suites 33 passed,
container wiring 12 passed. mypy --strict clean on 502 files. Constants
extractor reports no drift; formal/ untouched. registry lint --strict
clean on 269 files.

tasks.issue_text:
fix(security): refuse route_request without auth while a control is armed

Two P1s from the Codex review of #270, both confirmed and both the same
root cause: every control this container can arm keys on caller identity,
and the only production caller does not supply one.

  gate.py:62      user_id = auth.user_id if auth else ""
  gate.py:64,102  if self._strike_tracker and user_id:
  react.py:252    if sentinel is not None and auth is not None:
  adapters/maistro_core.py:180-184  route_request(messages, session_id=...,
                                    intent_hint=...)   # no auth

So with auth=None an armed permission table authorizes every tool and an
armed strike tracker records nothing -- silently, while the operator
believes enforcement is on. That is exactly the defect this batch exists
to fix (a live mechanism with no effect), reappearing one level up, and
it would have made the whole batch far less useful than its PR claimed.

route_request now raises AgentError when auth is None and either control
is armed, naming which one. At the shipped defaults the guard cannot fire
-- empty table, no tracker -- so no existing caller changes, including
hive-conductor's. It only fires for someone who explicitly opted in, and
for them a loud error beats silent non-enforcement.

Propagating a real AuthContext through hive-conductor's chat path is the
actual fix and belongs with the auth-surfaces work, not here; this guard
makes the gap impossible to ship unnoticed in the meantime.

Verified: 3 new tests (armed-table refused, armed-tracker refused,
defaults unaffected); container wiring 15 passed; core suite 5635 passed;
mypy --strict clean on 502 files.

tasks.issue_text:
fix(memory): exact org scoping and whitespace-tolerant delimiter filter

Addresses two P1 findings from the Codex review of #275, which merged
before they were resolved. Both are live on develop.

1. Cross-org learning exposure (persistence + agents/base)

   `find_relevant` and its siblings matched `(org_id = ? OR org_id = '')`,
   admitting every unowned row to every caller by analogy with the
   `agent_id = ''` convention. The analogy does not hold: `agent_id = ''`
   widens within one org, while `org_id = ''` crosses the tenancy
   boundary SPEC-216 lists as a non-goal ("cross-org learning sharing of
   any kind"). `InMemoryLearningStore` -- the reference implementation
   that spec describes -- already matched exactly; the SQL stores had
   drifted from it.

   It was reachable, not theoretical. `BaseAgent._extract_rca` populated
   `org_id`/`team_id` only on its traced branch, so with tracing disabled
   every RCA was stored unowned. A root-cause analysis derived from one
   org's tool failures then landed in every other org's *system prompt*,
   where a learning is an instruction rather than a datum.

   Both stores now match exactly, and the untraced branch sets the same
   scope fields as the traced one. Single-tenant deployments store "" and
   read "", so they are unaffected. Legacy rows predating the column
   backfill to "" and stay readable by that scope, but no longer become
   readable by an org -- unknown provenance is a reason to withhold, not
   to publish.

2. Delimiter filter bypass (agents/context_builder)

   `</?\s*maistro:` anchored the optional slash to `<`, so it stripped
   `</ maistro:corrections>` but left `< /maistro:corrections>` intact.
   The consumer is a delimiter-tolerant language model, not an XML
   parser, so the mirrored spelling is the same stored prompt-escape.
   Whitespace is now permitted on both sides of the slash.

Two scope tests reverse assertions they carried in #275
(`test_unowned_learnings_are_not_readable_by_an_org`, and the legacy-row
case in the schema-upgrade test). That reversal is the point: they
encoded the global-bucket contract this change removes.

Every new test was run against the unfixed source first and observed to
fail -- the regex cases on the mirrored spellings only, and the RCA cases
on 'org-1' != ''.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01T7hPwvJrRUN5iCNRQzCR1p

tasks.issue_text:
Report the terminalbench holdout, protect the measurement surface, fix the leaderboard

Three prerequisite fixes from the containment review's benchmark-realism plan
(§11.9 steps 2-3). None pays a capability bonus on its own; all three are on
the blocking path to one.

1. terminalbench: score the train and holdout splits separately

   `_TASKS = TRAINING_TASKS + HOLDOUT_TASKS` collapsed the split, so the one
   thing the split was built for -- detecting that a genome is memorizing the
   corpus rather than getting better at terminal work -- was averaged away
   before anyone could see it. Split membership is now resolved by task id, and
   metadata carries train_score / holdout_score / train_samples /
   holdout_samples / generalization_gap. Train rising while holdout stays flat
   is the memorization signature, and it is now visible in the result.

   The split is reported, not enforced: `_TASKS` is still the union, so fitness
   still sees the holdout. Three training tasks is too thin to drive a cycle
   from alone. What the docstring now states plainly is the consequence -- the
   combined score is contaminated by construction and must not pay a capability
   bonus. Only a holdout scored by a supervisor the loop cannot reach is
   bonus-eligible.

   Also counts errors. `except (TimeoutError, Exception)` scored a failed
   llm_call as 0.0, indistinguishable from a genuine wrong answer, so a
   degraded gateway read as a regression. metadata["errors"] separates them,
   and failures carry their split.

2. Put the measurement surface on the containment surface

   Everything already in SENSITIVE_PATH_PATTERNS governs what the loop may do.
   Nothing governed how the loop is scored, which is the same problem: a
   candidate that edits its own exam passes trivially and nothing notices.
   Added maistro_evolve/benchmarks/ (task corpora, graders, the split),
   maistro_evolve/fitness.py (breeding thresholds), scorecard.py,
   maistro_rsi/candidate_fitness.py and harvest.py (what gets promoted, what
   opens a PR) -- all of which were listed as improvement targets while
   unprotected.

   Also scripts/check_enumerations.py itself. `scripts/` matched no pattern, so
   a diff could edit the ratchet and the list it guards together and leave CI
   green. A guard outside the surface it guards is not a guard. SENSITIVE_ROOTS
   and SENSITIVE_FILES were extended to match so the ratchet holds the new
   entries; it passes with no new gaps.

   This escalates to adversarial review, it does not block -- and that
   escalation is still unwired on the shipped autorun path, tracked separately.

3. get_leaderboard: real battle counts, and stop mutating on read

   With benchmark=None it looked up a rating under the literal name "overall".
   No battle is ever recorded under that name, so every row reported
   total_battles=0 and win_rate=0.0 -- a genome with a perfect record read as
   unproven, and this is user-facing via GET /v1/tournament/leaderboard.

   Worse, _get_rating creates on miss, so reading the leaderboard inserted a
   phantom 1200-elo rating per genome. get_avg_elo averages over every rating
   for a genome, so a bare read moved it 1216.0 -> 1210.67 -- corrupting the
   number that feeds compute_fitness's elo component. Counts are now summed
   across the matched per-benchmark ratings via a throwaway aggregate, and

tasks.issue_text:
Make the hard fitness gate fail-closed, and drop osworld's unusable weight

Step 5 of the benchmark-realism plan, plus the unambiguous part of step 9.

The hard gate was inert for the entire RSI loop

`_check_hard_gate` iterated `_HARD_GATE_THRESHOLDS` and tested
`if bench in scores`. That correctly avoided penalising a subset run for
benchmarks it skipped — the bug it was written to fix — but it also meant any
benchmark ABSENT from the threshold dict passed unconditionally.

`code_rsi` was never in that dict, and it is the only benchmark the RSI loop
scores. So the gate never fired for self-improvement runs. Worse, `code_rsi`
collapses to exactly 0.0 when the fix is rejected or the test signal is stubbed
(`code_rsi.code_rsi_score`), so a genome whose fix was rejected outright still
bred, competing on cost, latency and diversity alone — the three components
that have nothing to do with whether it can fix code.

The gate now iterates the genome's scores rather than the threshold list, so
both properties hold together: a subset run is still not penalised for what it
skipped, and everything it did run is gated. Benchmarks with no tuned entry
fall back to `_DEFAULT_GATE_FLOOR` (0.01).

That floor is deliberately untuned. With no evidence about the composite
distribution, the only defensible universal claim is that a score of zero is a
total failure and must not breed; inventing a per-benchmark number would be
guessing. Replace it with a real entry once there is data — but fail closed
meanwhile, since the alternative is what this replaces.

Measured effect, old vs new:

  rejected RSI fix        breeds -> blocked   (fitness 0.00)
  stubbed RSI signal      breeds -> blocked   (fitness 0.00)
  custom benchmark @ 0.0  breeds -> blocked   (fitness 0.00)
  real RSI fix (0.636)    breeds -> breeds    (fitness 66.34)
  ifeval below its gate   blocked -> blocked

Only genomes scoring zero on an untuned benchmark change behaviour.

osworld's weight and floor removed

`run_osworld` raises NotImplementedError and is not registered, so its 0.05
`EvalWeights` entry and 0.15 gate threshold could never apply to a real score.
Weights are renormalised over the benchmarks that actually ran, so removing an
unusable entry changes no computed value — it just stops the model advertising
a benchmark this repo cannot run. Persisted genomes carrying an `osworld` key
still load; pydantic ignores the extra field.

The test that enumerated all 8 thresholds by hand — including osworld — is
replaced by one deriving coverage from `PROXY_BENCHMARKS`, so a newly
registered benchmark arriving without a threshold now fails the suite instead
of silently inheriting the floor. Same shape as the terminalbench test whose
name encoded the split collapse as intended behaviour.

GAIA and RAGAS, the rest of step 9, are left alone: dropping one and renaming
the other changes the registry's public surface and deserves a product call,
not a drive-by.

Tests: 1024 pass across maistro-evolve and maistro-rsi (6 new), 5730 in
maistro-core. ruff check ., ruff format --check, mypy --strict, both vendor
--checks, and the enumeration ratchet all pass.
